assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines Katori's magic-wavelength proposal with Ye's realization of clocks at the 10^-18 level. It is a measurement instrument that changed what can be measured: relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants, searches for dark matter and a coming redefinition of the second. Impact is strong across atomic physics and beyond, and the experimental demonstrations are thorough.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrated it. Ye's group drove the accuracy and stability records and the many-body (Sr lattice) clock. A two-person prize is natural and within the supplied names. Ye was not a laureate in the 2005 frequency-comb prize (Hall and Hänsch were), so I see no conflict. Other contributors, such as Pierre Lemonde's group, are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Several independent labs (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) have confirmed and surpassed the early results. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with ion-clock work (Wineland, 2012 prize) and the frequency comb (2005 prize) may make some members feel the area is already honored.
Whether a Nobel would be given for the clock itself or for the underlying lattice trapping idea is an open framing question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry gives inertial sensing, gravimetry, gradiometry and constant measurements (G, alpha) with extraordinary sensitivity. It matches the view that progress is limited by how precisely we can measure. Applications range from mineral exploration to tests of equivalence principle, and the method is a platform for tests of fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard first demonstrated atom interferometers with material gratings, Bordé gave the theoretical and spectroscopic foundations (Ramsey-Bordé), and Kasevich built the first precision gravimeters and gyroscopes. All three have defensible claims and fit the three-person limit. Credit of Chu, Chapman, Rasel and others is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature and independently confirmed by many groups, with commercial gravimeters in use. Large-scale fundamental-physics applications are still under development.
uncertainties: Steven Chu's role, partly honored in 1997, and other group leaders are outside the supplied credit list, so the fairness of the trio is uncertain.
Some applications (equivalence principle tests at scale) are still prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single NV centers opened room-temperature quantum sensing of magnetic fields, temperature and electric fields at nanometer scale, with uses in biology and materials. The experimental route from single-spin detection to practical sensors is clear and well documented.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated optical readout of single NV spins and their coherent control; Lukin led much of the quantum-sensing and multi-qubit register development with NV centers. This is a reasonable trio, though Lukin's strongest claim lies partly in other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduce the results and sensing is used across fields. The impact on measurement is concrete, though some applications are still being established.
uncertainties: Sensitivity advantage over other magnetometers is application-dependent and still debated.
Allocation of credit between sensing and quantum-register work is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Electromagnetically induced transparency and slow and stopped light are conceptually elegant and underpin quantum memories and nonlinear optics at single-photon level. As someone who works with slow light and spectral holes, I see the lasting methods impact, though it is more concept than final application.
assessment.attribution: Harris developed the theory and first demonstrations of EIT; Hau's group demonstrated ultraslow and stopped light in a condensate. Two laureates from the supplied names appear sufficient. Imamoglu's contribution is real but less decisive for the core discovery. Credit to Fleischhauer, Lukin and Boller is not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed repeatedly in vapors, condensates and solids; interpretation stable. The field is mature, though applications have grown more slowly than first projected.
uncertainties: Attribution between the early theory of dark states (Arimondo, Alzetta, others) and EIT is not on the list and may be contested.
Real-world device impact is smaller than the conceptual impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atoms in optical lattices realized Hubbard-model physics, the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and single-site quantum gas microscopy, enabling quantum simulation with controllable parameters. It is a major platform for many-body physics and measurement of correlations.
assessment.attribution: Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition and developed the quantum-gas microscope; Esslinger demonstrated fermionic Mott insulators and related work. Zoller's theoretical proposal (with Jaksch) is foundational, so the choice among four names is hard. I choose the experimental trio, but would also support a theory plus experiment pairing.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups, though the sharpest goals (solving open Hubbard-model problems) are not yet reached.
uncertainties: Zoller's theory credit versus Greiner's or Esslinger's experiments is unresolved with a limit of three names.
Quantum simulation has not yet delivered answers to open problems at the highest expected level.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light reduces quantum noise below the standard limit and is now routinely used in gravitational-wave detectors, an unusually concrete case of quantum-enhanced measurement. Caves provided the interferometer proposal, and the experimental demonstrations are clear.
assessment.attribution: Caves proposed squeezed-state interferometry; Kimble's group generated the first squeezed light, and Schnabel's group pioneered the audio-band squeezing suited to GEO600 and LIGO. Slusher, Wu and others also made early demonstrations, not on the list, which complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed by deployment in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Early experimental credit to Slusher, Wu and Walls groups is outside the list.
Whether a prize should recognize generation, proposal or deployment is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson required extraordinary detector and instrument development and completed the Standard Model. Importance is not in doubt. From an experimentalist perspective the detector-technology achievement is impressive.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize went to the theorists. The experimental recognition is hard because the collaborations have thousands of members; the supplied credit names (spokespersons and conveners, plus the LHC project leader Lyn Evans) are a choice of leadership, not individual discovery. Prize rules favor a small trio, making allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two independent experiments and years of follow-up. Very mature.
uncertainties: Attributing a collaboration discovery to three individuals is contentious.
The prize for the theoretical prediction was already given in 2013, which may reduce appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos, and the identification of the first sources (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068), opened neutrino astronomy through a cubic-kilometer instrument built in Antarctic ice. It is a major new window of observation.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the driving force for IceCube; Karle and Spiering made key contributions to the design and analysis. Large-collaboration attribution is an issue, and Karle and Spiering are among several plausible people.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established; source identification is still evolving, so some interpretation is not yet stable. Moderately timely, probably slightly early.
uncertainties: Source-level identifications are few and statistical significance is moderate.
Collaboration credit among more than three leaders is not clearly resolved.
